title: Pokemon Ruby Version
sources: pret/pokeruby decompilation (GitHub): trainer parties (src/data/trainers.h, trainer_parties.h), map scripts, hidden items (map.json bg_events), evolutions, wild encounters, roamer.c
The English ROM itself (AXVE): region map section names and trainer names/levels, read on the PC with ui/src/pokemon.cpp (findTables) - the ground truth for every place name and level cap
Bulbapedia (bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net): Courtney, Tabitha, Team Magma Hideout pages, read through a web search summary (admin roles per version)
pret/pokeemerald and pret/pokefirered src/link.c, pret/pokeruby src/trade.c: a trade with FireRed/LeafGreen/Emerald turns on the National Pokédex

milestones.name: Rival: first battle (Route 103)
milestones.tips: Your neighbour uses the starter that is strong against yours, at Level 5. Two or three levels on Route 101 or 103 first make it easy; heal at Oldale's Pokémon Center.

milestones.name: Team Magma grunt in Petalburg Woods
milestones.tips: A lone grunt with a Level 9 Poochyena tries to rob a Devon researcher. Any Pokémon around Level 10 wins; the researcher gives you a Great Ball.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby (Petalburg Woods grunt); pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc

milestones.name: Gym 1: Roxanne
milestones.badge_note: Stone Badge: Cut works in the field (HM01 from the Cutter's house in Rustboro). Gym TM: TM39 Rock Tomb.
milestones.tips: Rock types: Geodude at 14 and Nosepass at 15 with Rock Tomb. Water and Grass moves win (Mudkip, Treecko, Lotad, Shroomish); Torchic needs a partner, or a Fighting move after it evolves.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby; HM checks in src/party_menu.c

milestones.name: Get the Devon Goods back (Rusturf Tunnel)
milestones.tips: The grunt who stole the Devon Goods waits in Rusturf Tunnel east of Rustboro with a Level 11 Poochyena. Mr. Stone then gives you a letter for Steven and the PokéNav.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby (Rusturf Tunnel grunt); pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc

milestones.name: Gym 2: Brawly
milestones.badge_note: Knuckle Badge: Flash works in the field, and traded Pokémon up to Level 30 obey. Gym TM: TM08 Bulk Up.
milestones.tips: Fighting types: Machop at 17 and Makuhita at 18 with Bulk Up. Flying (Taillow, Wingull) and Psychic (Kirlia) moves win. Get Flash from the hiker in Granite Cave first to light the cave.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby; obedience in src/battle_util.c

milestones.name: Deliver the letter to Steven (Granite Cave)
milestones.tips: Mr. Briney sails you to Dewford. Steven waits at the far end of Granite Cave's first floors; the lower floors' cracked tiles need the Mach Bike, but only for items. He gives TM47 Steel Wing.

milestones.name: Team Magma at the Oceanic Museum (Slateport)
milestones.tips: Two grunts (Level 14 and 15 Pokémon) corner Captain Stern on the museum's 2nd floor when you bring the Devon Goods. The museum charges a small entry fee.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby (museum grunts); pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc

milestones.name: Rival: Route 110
milestones.tips: Three Pokémon, the starter at 20. After the fight the rival gives you the Itemfinder. Cycling Road above the route needs a bike (Rydel's shop in Mauville).

milestones.name: Wally in Mauville City
milestones.tips: Wally wants to prove himself with his Ralts (Level 16) at the gym door. Any of your Pokémon wins; after this Wally moves to Verdanturf.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby MauvilleCity scripts (Wally there from the start)

milestones.name: Gym 3: Wattson
milestones.badge_note: Dynamo Badge: Rock Smash works in the field (HM06 from a house in Mauville). Gym TM: TM34 Shock Wave.
milestones.tips: Electric types: Magnemite 22, Voltorb 20, Magneton 23. Ground moves are the answer (Geodude from Granite Cave, Marshtomp); Magnemite and Magneton are also part Steel.

milestones.name: The Winstrate family (Route 111)
milestones.tips: Four battles in a row on Route 111: Victor (Taillow, Zigzagoon at 16), Victoria (Roselia 17), Vivi (Marill, Shroomish, Numel at 15) and Vicky (Meditite 18). Leave before beating Vicky and the series starts over. Win all four and the family gives you the Macho Brace.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby Route111 and Route111_WinstrateFamilysHouse scripts

milestones.name: Stop Team Magma at Mt. Chimney
milestones.tips: Take the cable car up from Route 112 (the Meteor Falls scene sends you there). A grunt and then the admin Tabitha (Level 20) stand between you and the leader at the summit machine. Water and Ground moves cover most of it.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc (MT_CHIMNEY_GRUNT_1/2)

milestones.name: Maxie at Mt. Chimney
milestones.tips: The leader himself guards the machine: Mightyena and Golbat at 24, Camerupt at 25. Camerupt is Fire/Ground, so Water moves hit it four times as hard. Electric, Ice, Psychic or Rock moves for Golbat.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc (MT_CHIMNEY_GRUNT_3 = MAXIE_3)

milestones.name: Gym 4: Flannery
milestones.badge_note: Heat Badge: Strength works in the field (HM04 in Rusturf Tunnel), and traded Pokémon up to Level 50 obey. Gym TM: TM50 Overheat.
milestones.tips: Two Slugma at 26 and a Torkoal at 28 with Overheat. Water moves win easily; Rock and Ground also hit hard.

milestones.name: Gym 5: Norman (your father)
milestones.badge_note: Balance Badge: Surf works in the field (HM03 from Wally's father in Petalburg right after). Gym TM: TM42 Facade.
milestones.tips: Slaking 28, Vigoroth 30, Slaking 31. Slaking loafs every other turn (Truant): set up or switch on those turns. Fighting moves (Combusken, Breloom, Makuhita) win.

milestones.name: New Mauville for Wattson
milestones.tips: After the Balance Badge, Wattson waits outside Mauville's gym and gives you the Basement Key. New Mauville is reached by water from Route 110. Floor switches raise and lower the barriers; the switch by the generator shuts it down. Voltorb (Level 25) pose as items. Wattson then gives you TM24 Thunderbolt.
milestones.source: pret/pokeruby MauvilleCity, NewMauville_Inside scripts; PetalburgCity_Gym (Wattson leaves the gym after badge 5)

milestones.name: Team Magma raid the Weather Institute (Route 119)
milestones.tips: Grunts at 26-28 on both floors, then the admin Courtney with two Level 28 Pokémon. Win and the institute gives you a Castform.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby; Bulbapedia: Courtney (via search)

milestones.name: Rival: Route 119
milestones.tips: Three Pokémon with the starter's second form at 31. The rival then hands over HM02 Fly, which needs the Feather Badge.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby (*_ROUTE_119_*); HM02 in Route119 scripts

milestones.name: Gym 6: Winona
milestones.badge_note: Feather Badge: Fly works in the field, traded Pokémon up to Level 70 obey. Gym TM: TM40 Aerial Ace. An invisible Kecleon blocks the way until Steven gives you the Devon Scope on Route 120.
milestones.tips: Swellow 31, Pelipper 30, Skarmory 32, Altaria 33. Electric moves for the birds, Fire for Skarmory, Ice or Rock for Altaria.

milestones.name: Rival: Lilycove City
milestones.tips: The last rival fight: four Pokémon, the starter at 34. After it the rival no longer battles you.

milestones.name: Mt. Pyre summit
milestones.tips: Team Magma grunts block the path to the summit, and the leader takes one of the two orbs kept by the old couple. The trail then leads to Slateport's harbor.

milestones.name: The stolen submarine (Slateport harbor)
milestones.tips: After Mt. Pyre, go to Slateport's harbor: Team Magma takes Captain Stern's submarine and Maxie boasts that the team's hideout is in Lilycove. The grunts who blocked the hideout's entrance are gone after this.

milestones.name: Team Magma Hideout (east of Lilycove)
milestones.tips: Surf east of Lilycove to the cave. Warp panels lead to the admin (Tabitha, three Pokémon at 32). The leader escapes in the stolen submarine. A Master Ball is on B1F.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby; pret/pokeruby item_ball_scripts.inc (Master Ball)

milestones.name: Gym 7: Tate & Liza
milestones.badge_note: Mind Badge: Dive works in the field (HM08 from Steven at his house in Mossdeep). Gym TM: TM04 Calm Mind.
milestones.tips: A double battle with Lunatone and Solrock at 42. Water and Grass moves hit both hard; Surf hits both at once. Watch for Sunny Day and Solar Beam.

milestones.name: Seafloor Cavern
milestones.tips: Dive on Route 128 to find the cavern. Strength and Rock Smash puzzles lead past grunts (36-38) to the admin Courtney (Camerupt and Mightyena at 38); the leader waits in the deepest room.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc (SEAFLOOR_CAVERN_GRUNT_3)

milestones.name: Maxie in the Seafloor Cavern
milestones.tips: Mightyena and Crobat at 41, Camerupt at 43. Water moves hit Camerupt four times as hard. Psychic, Ice, Electric or Rock for Crobat; Fighting or Bug for Mightyena. After this the legend wakes.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby constants/version.inc (SEAFLOOR_CAVERN_GRUNT_5 = MAXIE_2)

milestones.name: Groudon (Cave of Origin)
milestones.tips: After the Seafloor Cavern, Groudon goes to the Cave of Origin under Sootopolis. Steven and Wallace let you in; it waits at the bottom at Level 45. Save first; Ultra Balls and a status move help.

milestones.name: Gym 8: Wallace
milestones.badge_note: Rain Badge: Waterfall works in the field (HM07 lies in the Cave of Origin), and every traded Pokémon obeys. Gym TM: TM03 Water Pulse.
milestones.tips: Water types: Luvdisc 40, Whiscash 42 (Ground, immune to Electric), Sealeo 40, Seaking 42 and Milotic 43, which can recover. Grass moves hit all but Sealeo (Water/Ice: use Electric or Fighting on it).
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby; pret/pokeruby item_ball_scripts.inc (HM07)

milestones.name: Wally at Victory Road
milestones.tips: Wally blocks the way in Victory Road with Gardevoir at 45 and Altaria, Delcatty, Roselia and Magneton. Fire beats Roselia, Ice beats Altaria, Ground beats Magneton.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby (Wally, Victory Road)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Sidney
milestones.tips: Dark types up to Absol 49 (Mightyena, Shiftry, Cacturne, Sharpedo). Fighting and Bug moves; Shiftry and Cacturne fear Fire, Ice and Flying.

milestones.name: Elite Four: Phoebe
milestones.tips: Ghosts: two Dusclops, two Banette, Sableye. Dark and Ghost moves work; Normal and Fighting don't touch them. Sableye has no weakness in Gen III.

milestones.name: Elite Four: Glacia
milestones.tips: Ice: Glalie and Sealeo twice, Walrein 53. Fire, Fighting, Rock, Steel and Electric (for Sealeo/Walrein) moves. Hail chips your team.

milestones.name: Elite Four: Drake
milestones.tips: Dragons: Shelgon, Altaria, two Flygon, Salamence 55. Ice moves are four times as strong on Altaria, Flygon and Salamence.

milestones.name: Champion Steven
milestones.tips: Steel and Rock: Skarmory 57, Claydol 55, Aggron, Cradily, Armaldo 56, Metagross 58. Ground and Water moves hit most; Fire for Skarmory and Metagross, Ice for Claydol.

milestones.name: Wally after the Hall of Fame (Victory Road)
milestones.tips: After the Hall of Fame Wally waits on Victory Road's first floor: Gardevoir 48 with Altaria, Delcatty, Roselia and Magneton. When he wants a rematch later his team grows, up to Gardevoir at 57.
milestones.source: ROM AXVE trainer table; pret/pokeruby VictoryRoad_1F, hall_of_fame.inc, src/battle_setup.c (Wally rematches)

milestones.name: Rayquaza (Sky Pillar)
milestones.tips: After the Hall of Fame, Sky Pillar on Route 131 opens. Climb with the Mach Bike over the cracked floors; Rayquaza waits on top at Level 70.

milestones.name: Battle Tower
milestones.tips: The S.S. Tidal (Slateport or Lilycove) takes you to the Battle Tower after the Hall of Fame. Pick three Pokémon; rounds of seven battles at Level 50 or open level.

milestones.name: The three Regis
milestones.tips: Dive on Route 134 to the Sealed Chamber. With Relicanth first and Wailord last in your party the Braille wall opens, and the caves of Regirock (Desert Ruins), Regice (Island Cave) and Registeel (Ancient Tomb) unlock. Each is Level 40.
milestones.source: pret/pokeruby SealedChamber, DesertRuins, IslandCave, AncientTomb scripts

milestones.name: Regirock (Desert Ruins)
milestones.tips: After the Sealed Chamber, enter the Desert Ruins in Route 111's sandstorm. The Braille asks for Strength: use it in front of the wall and the inner room opens. Regirock waits at Level 40; save first.

milestones.name: Regice (Island Cave)
milestones.tips: The Island Cave is on Route 105. Its Braille says to wait: stand still for two minutes without pressing a button and the wall opens. Regice waits at Level 40.

milestones.name: Registeel (Ancient Tomb)
milestones.tips: The Ancient Tomb is on Route 120. The Braille says to aim for the sky in the middle: use Fly from the field menu in the middle of the room and the wall opens. Registeel waits at Level 40.

milestones.name: Roaming Latios
milestones.tips: After the Hall of Fame your mother's TV report sets Latios roaming Hoenn at Level 40. It flees on the first turn; trap it (Mean Look, Wobbuffet's Shadow Tag) or put it to sleep.

steps.title: Pick a starter on Route 101
steps.text: Rescue Professor Birch from a Poochyena and pick Treecko, Torchic or Mudkip from his bag. Mudkip has the easiest first two gyms; Torchic the hardest.

steps.title: Help Wally catch Ralts
steps.text: In Petalburg your father asks you to go with Wally to Route 102, where he catches a Ralts. You then get your first chance at Poké Balls in the Mart.

steps.title: Catch a team for Roxanne
steps.text: Good early catches: Seedot on Route 102, Shroomish in Petalburg Woods, Wingull on Route 104. A Water or Grass move makes Roxanne easy.

steps.title: Devon Goods, the letter and the PokéNav
steps.text: After the Rusturf Tunnel grunt, Mr. Stone (Devon Corp. top floor) gives you the PokéNav and a letter for Steven. Mr. Briney on Route 104 sails you to Dewford.

steps.title: Exp. Share from Mr. Stone
steps.text: Come back to Devon Corp.'s top floor after delivering the letter: Mr. Stone gives you the Exp. Share. Hold it on a weak Pokémon to train it without battling.

steps.title: Get a bike in Mauville
steps.text: Rydel's Cycles gives you a free bike: the Mach Bike (speed, cracked floors, slopes) or the Acro Bike (rails, jumps). You can swap at any time in the shop.

steps.title: Meteor Falls and the cable car
steps.text: On Route 114 to Meteor Falls you see Team Magma take the meteorite, then follow them through Route 112's cable car up Mt. Chimney.

steps.title: Go-Goggles for the desert
steps.text: After Flannery, the rival in Lavaridge gives you the Go-Goggles. You need them to cross the sandstorm on Route 111 (desert, fossils, Trapinch).

steps.title: Surf, then the sea routes
steps.text: Wally's father gives you HM03 Surf in Petalburg right after Norman. Surf opens Route 105-109's water, Route 118 east and the way north.

steps.title: Devon Scope for the Kecleon
steps.text: An invisible Pokémon blocks Fortree's gym. Steven waits on Route 120's bridge: he reveals a hidden Kecleon there, which battles you (Level 30), then gives you the Devon Scope. Use it on the blocked spot in Fortree and that Kecleon runs off.

steps.title: Dive and the deep sea
steps.text: Steven gives you HM08 Dive at his house in Mossdeep. Dark patches in the sea let you dive: the way to the Seafloor Cavern is on Route 128.

steps.title: Victory Road needs Waterfall
steps.text: Victory Road and Ever Grande City need Surf, Waterfall, Strength and Rock Smash. Bring a team around Level 50 and many Hyper Potions; there is no healing in the league.

steps.title: The Elite Four in one go
steps.text: The Elite Four are fought back to back with no Pokémon Center between them. A healthy level-50+ team with type coverage for Dark, Ghost, Ice and Dragon, plus Full Restores, is the plan.

steps.title: National Pokédex
steps.text: Ruby and Sapphire have no in-game upgrade: the National Pokédex switches on after a trade with FireRed, LeafGreen or Emerald (any of them signals it over the link). Those trades are then the way to fill it.

steps.title: Pokémon Contests
steps.text: The Contest Halls in Verdanturf, Fallarbor, Slateport and Lilycove take Pokémon with high condition. Feed Pokéblocks made from berries at the Berry Blender. Winning ranks unlocks ribbons and paintings.

steps.title: Plant berries
steps.text: Soft soil on routes takes berries. They grow in a few hours and bear several fruit; water them with the Wailmer Pail (from the berry shop on Route 104) for more.

steps.title: Secret Base
steps.text: A boy on Route 111 gives you TM43 Secret Power. Use it on a hollow tree, a bush or a hole in a rock wall to make a base and decorate it; mixing records shares bases.

steps.title: Trick House on Route 110
steps.text: The Trick Master's house on Route 110 sets a new puzzle after each badge. Each finished puzzle gives an item.

steps.title: PokéNav
steps.text: The PokéNav from Mr. Stone has the region map, a condition screen for contests and Trainer's Eyes: it marks trainers who want a rematch.

steps.title: Weather-legend prep
steps.text: These legends hit hard and some heal themselves. Bring Ultra Balls, Timer Balls (better each turn) and a Pokémon with a sleep or paralysis move.
steps.source: pret/pokeruby static wild battles, src/battle_script_commands.c (ball multipliers)

steps.title: Rayquaza needs the Mach Bike
steps.text: Sky Pillar's upper floors have cracked tiles: ride the Mach Bike over them without stopping. Save before the top.

steps.title: The Scanner on the Abandoned Ship
steps.text: The Abandoned Ship on Route 108 has a flooded hidden floor you reach with Dive. Keys found on board open its locked rooms, and one holds the Scanner. A sailor in the Captain's Office asks you to take it to Captain Stern at Slateport's harbor, who swaps it for a Deep Sea Tooth or a Deep Sea Scale.

steps.title: Relicanth and Wailord for the Sealed Chamber
steps.text: The Sealed Chamber wants Relicanth first and Wailord last in your party. Relicanth lives underwater (Dive); Wailmer, common on the sea routes, becomes Wailord at Level 40.
steps.source: pret/pokeruby src/braille_puzzles.c (CheckRelicanthWailord); ROM AXVE wild data and evolutions

The Weather Institute gives you a Castform (Level 25) after you drive Team Magma out. Its form follows the weather.
An old woman by the hot springs in Lavaridge Town gives you an Egg; it hatches into Wynaut.
After the Hall of Fame, Steven's house in Mossdeep holds a Poké Ball with a Beldum (Level 5) left for you.
In Route 111's desert (Go-Goggles) two fossils lie side by side: Root Fossil (Lileep) and Claw Fossil (Anorith). Taking one makes the other sink. Devon in Rustboro revives it.
Mr. Stone gives you the Exp. Share on Devon Corp.'s top floor after Steven gets the letter.
The chairman of the Pokémon Fan Club in Slateport gives a Soothe Bell when your lead is friendly enough. Hold it to raise friendship faster (Golbat, Azurill, Pichu and co.).
Beat the Winstrate family four times in a row in their house on Route 111 and they give you the Macho Brace (double effort points, half Speed while held).
A boy in Mossdeep City gives you a King's Rock. Held when traded, it turns Poliwhirl into Politoed and Slowpoke into Slowking.
A man at the Mossdeep Space Center gives you a Sun Stone (Gloom to Bellossom, Sunkern to Sunflora).
The Scanner lies in the Abandoned Ship's sunken rooms (Dive). Give it to Captain Stern at Slateport Harbor and pick a Deep Sea Tooth or Deep Sea Scale for Clamperl.
The treasure hunter's house on Route 124 swaps colored shards for evolution stones: red for Fire, blue for Water, yellow for Thunder, green for Leaf.
Feebas only bites on six hidden water tiles of Route 119 (fish with any rod). The tiles change when the trend phrase in Lilycove changes. Raise its Beauty with dry Pokéblocks to evolve it.
Mirage Island rises off Route 130 only on days when a random daily number matches one of your Pokémon. It has Wynaut and Liechi Berries; an old man in Pacifidlog says when it can be seen.
The invisible Kecleon on Route 120 (Devon Scope) battle you at Level 30; you can catch them.
Two Poké Balls in the Magma Hideout are Electrode (Level 30) in disguise.
New Mauville (Route 110, Basement Key from Wattson) has Electrode and Voltorb disguised as items.
Shoal Cave off Mossdeep changes with the tide every six hours. At low tide collect Shoal Salt and Shoal Shells; four of each make a Shell Bell. Snorunt lives in the ice room.
The Safari Zone (Route 121) is the only place for Pikachu, Girafarig, Doduo, Phanpy and Heracross in Hoenn. Pokéblock feeders attract Pokémon of one nature.
Bagon lives only in a back room of Meteor Falls (needs Surf and Waterfall). Shelgon evolves at 30, Salamence at 50.
Absol appears only on Route 120's grass. Chimecho lives at Mt. Pyre's summit; Tropius on Route 119's tall grass.
The Cutter's house in Rustboro gives HM01 Cut; it needs the Stone Badge.
A hiker on Granite Cave's first floor gives HM05 Flash; it needs the Knuckle Badge.
A man in a Mauville house gives HM06 Rock Smash; it needs the Dynamo Badge.
Once the tunnel is clear, a man in Rusturf Tunnel gives HM04 Strength; it needs the Heat Badge.
HM07 Waterfall lies in an item ball deep in the Cave of Origin, on the way to Groudon.
A Master Ball lies in an item ball on the hideout's B1F. Two other balls are Electrode in disguise.
Southern Island holds Latias at Level 50, but only with the Eon Ticket from an event; normal play never opens it.

evolutions.name: Kadabra
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade over the Game Link Cable (Ruby/Sapphire do not support the Wireless Adapter). Hoenn has Abra in Granite Cave in the wild.

evolutions.name: Machoke
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade over the Game Link Cable (Ruby/Sapphire do not support the Wireless Adapter). Hoenn has Machop on Fiery Path and Jagged Pass (and Route 112) in the wild.

evolutions.name: Graveler
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade over the Game Link Cable (Ruby/Sapphire do not support the Wireless Adapter). Hoenn has Geodude in Granite Cave and on Routes 111 and 114 in the wild.

evolutions.name: Haunter
evolutions.text: Evolves only through a link trade over the Game Link Cable (Ruby/Sapphire do not support the Wireless Adapter). Hoenn has no Gastly; trade one in from FireRed/LeafGreen in the wild.

evolutions.name: Poliwhirl
evolutions.text: A Water Stone gives Poliwrath; trading it while it holds a King's Rock (from a boy in Mossdeep) gives Politoed. Poliwag is not wild in Hoenn.

evolutions.name: Slowpoke
evolutions.text: Level 37 gives Slowbro; trading it while it holds a King's Rock gives Slowking.

evolutions.name: Onix
evolutions.text: Evolves into Steelix when traded holding a Metal Coat. A few wild Magnemite and Magneton in New Mauville carry one: take it with Thief or Covet.

evolutions.name: Scyther
evolutions.text: Evolves into Scizor when traded holding a Metal Coat.

evolutions.name: Seadra
evolutions.text: Evolves into Kingdra when traded holding a Dragon Scale (carried by some wild Horsea and Seadra on Routes 132-134).

evolutions.name: Porygon
evolutions.text: Evolves into Porygon2 when traded holding an Up-Grade; neither Porygon nor the Up-Grade exists in Hoenn, so both come from FireRed/LeafGreen.

evolutions.name: Clamperl
evolutions.text: Traded holding the Deep Sea Tooth it becomes Huntail; holding the Deep Sea Scale, Gorebyss. Captain Stern gives one of them for the Scanner.

evolutions.name: Feebas
evolutions.text: Evolves into Milotic on a level-up once its Beauty condition is high (170). Raise Beauty with dry, blue-flavoured Pokéblocks; berries like Wepear and Pamtre help.

evolutions.name: Golbat
evolutions.text: Evolves into Crobat on a level-up with high friendship (220). Walking with it, battling and the Soothe Bell raise it.

evolutions.name: Azurill
evolutions.text: Evolves into Marill on a level-up with high friendship. Marill becomes Azumarill at Level 18.

evolutions.name: Pichu
evolutions.text: Evolves into Pikachu with high friendship. Pikachu then needs a Thunder Stone.

evolutions.name: Igglybuff
evolutions.text: Evolves into Jigglypuff with high friendship; a Moon Stone then gives Wigglytuff.

evolutions.name: Cleffa
evolutions.text: Evolves into Clefairy with high friendship; a Moon Stone then gives Clefable.

evolutions.name: Togepi
evolutions.text: Evolves into Togetic with high friendship. Togekiss does not exist yet.

evolutions.name: Chansey
evolutions.text: Evolves into Blissey on a level-up with high friendship. Chansey is not wild in Hoenn: trade one from FireRed/LeafGreen.

evolutions.name: Eevee
evolutions.text: Fire, Water or Thunder Stone for Flareon, Vaporeon, Jolteon. High friendship on a level-up from 12:00 to 23:59 gives Espeon, from 0:00 to 11:59 Umbreon (the game's clock). No Leafeon/Glaceon in Gen III.

evolutions.name: Gloom
evolutions.text: Leaf Stone gives Vileplume; Sun Stone (Mossdeep Space Center) gives Bellossom. Oddish lives on Routes 110, 117, 119-123.

evolutions.name: Sunkern
evolutions.text: A Sun Stone turns it into Sunflora.

evolutions.name: Tyrogue
evolutions.text: At Level 20: Attack higher than Defense gives Hitmonlee, lower gives Hitmonchan, equal gives Hitmontop.

evolutions.name: Wurmple
evolutions.text: At Level 7 it becomes Silcoon (then Beautifly) or Cascoon (then Dustox). A hidden personality value decides; you cannot pick.

evolutions.name: Nincada
evolutions.text: At Level 20 it becomes Ninjask; if you have a free party slot and a spare Poké Ball, a Shedinja appears in that slot too.

evolutions.name: Lombre
evolutions.text: A Water Stone evolves it into Ludicolo.

evolutions.name: Nuzleaf
evolutions.text: A Leaf Stone evolves it into Shiftry.

evolutions.name: Skitty
evolutions.text: A Moon Stone evolves it into Delcatty. Moon Stones are found in Meteor Falls.

evolutions.name: Kirlia
evolutions.text: Level 30 gives Gardevoir. Gallade (Dawn Stone) does not exist in Gen III.

evolutions.name: Snorunt
evolutions.text: Level 42 gives Glalie. Froslass does not exist in Gen III.

evolutions.name: Roselia
evolutions.text: Roselia does not evolve in Gen III (no Budew or Roserade yet).

evolutions.name: Dusclops
evolutions.text: Dusclops does not evolve in Gen III (Dusknoir came later). Duskull evolves into it at 37.

evolutions.name: Shelgon
evolutions.text: Level 50 gives Salamence; Bagon becomes Shelgon at 30.

evolutions.name: Metang
evolutions.text: Level 45 gives Metagross; Beldum becomes Metang at 20 (Beldum only knows Take Down until then).

evolutions.name: Spheal
evolutions.text: Level 32 gives Sealeo, Level 44 Walrein.

evolutions.name: Trapinch
evolutions.text: Level 35 gives Vibrava, Level 45 Flygon.

evolutions.name: Swablu
evolutions.text: Level 35 gives Altaria.

evolutions.name: Lileep
evolutions.text: Level 40 gives Cradily. Anorith becomes Armaldo at 40 too.

evolutions.name: Magikarp
evolutions.text: Level 20 gives Gyarados. An old rod in Dewford catches Magikarp right away.

evolutions.name: Shroomish
evolutions.text: Level 23 gives Breloom (Grass/Fighting).

evolutions.name: Makuhita
evolutions.text: Level 24 gives Hariyama.

evolutions.name: Aron
evolutions.text: Level 32 gives Lairon, Level 42 Aggron.

evolutions.name: Electrike
evolutions.text: Level 26 gives Manectric.

evolutions.name: Numel
evolutions.text: Level 33 gives Camerupt.

evolutions.name: Slakoth
evolutions.text: Level 18 gives Vigoroth, Level 36 Slaking (Truant: it acts every other turn).

evolutions.name: Ralts
evolutions.text: Level 20 gives Kirlia.

evolutions.name: Whismur
evolutions.text: Level 20 gives Loudred, Level 40 Exploud.

evolutions.name: Carvanha
evolutions.text: Level 30 gives Sharpedo.

evolutions.name: Wailmer
evolutions.text: Level 40 gives Wailord, which you need for the Regi puzzle.

notes.title: Only in Ruby
notes.text: Found only in this version: Seedot, Nuzleaf, Shiftry, Mawile, Zangoose, Solrock, Groudon.

notes.title: Trade from Sapphire
notes.text: These come only from Sapphire (or Emerald for some): Lotad, Lombre, Ludicolo, Sableye, Seviper, Lunatone, Kyogre.

notes.title: Legendaries in this game
notes.text: Groudon (Cave of Origin, 45), Rayquaza (Sky Pillar after the Hall of Fame, 70), the Regis (40), and Latios roaming (40). Kyogre and Jirachi/Deoxys need trades or events.

notes.title: Latios roams
notes.text: After the Hall of Fame Latios roams Hoenn's routes at Level 40. It changes route whenever you change maps and flees at once; the Pokédex area map shows where it is.

notes.title: Your villain team
notes.text: Pokemon Ruby Version has Team Magma as the main villains (they want to raise the land). The other team appears too and is beaten by them in the story.

notes.title: The in-game clock
notes.text: Berries, tides, Mirage Island and Espeon/Umbreon use the cartridge's real-time clock. On an emulator the clock follows the host; old carts with a dead battery stop berry growth.

notes.title: Trading with FireRed and LeafGreen
notes.text: After the National Pokédex you can trade with FireRed/LeafGreen (they need the Sevii Islands' network machine first). This is the way to get Kanto and Johto Pokémon and starters.
notes.source: pret/pokeruby cable club scripts; pret/pokefirered OneIsland scripts

notes.title: Physical or special by type
notes.text: In Gen III a move's type decides whether it is physical or special: Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Ice, Psychic, Dragon and Dark are special; the rest are physical. A Dark move uses Sp. Atk.

notes.title: Abilities and natures are new
notes.text: Gen III added abilities and natures. A nature raises one stat by 10% and lowers another; Synchronize (Ralts, Kirlia) in the lead makes wild natures match half of the time.

notes.title: Berries never grow?
notes.text: Ruby and Sapphire had a clock bug that stopped berry growth a year after the start; the game's 'Berry Program Update' fixes it. Emerald does not have the bug.

notes.title: HM list
notes.text: Cut (Rustboro), Fly (rival, Route 119), Surf (Petalburg), Strength (Rusturf Tunnel), Flash (Granite Cave), Rock Smash (Mauville), Dive (Steven, Mossdeep), Waterfall (Cave of Origin). HM moves can only be removed by the Move Deleter in Lilycove.

notes.title: Pokéblocks and condition
notes.text: Pokéblocks raise Cool, Beauty, Cute, Smart and Tough. A Pokémon's Sheen caps how many it eats. Dry (blue) blocks raise Beauty, which Feebas needs.

notes.title: Rare Candies, PP Ups: where
notes.text: Hidden items are worth hunting with the Itemfinder from the rival: Rare Candies lie hidden on Routes 108, 111, 120, at Mt. Pyre's summit and in Petalburg City.

notes.title: Starters' types
notes.text: Treecko (Grass) becomes Sceptile, Torchic (Fire) becomes Blaziken (Fire/Fighting), Mudkip (Water) becomes Swampert (Water/Ground, only weak to Grass).

notes.title: Weather
notes.text: Rain, sun, sandstorm and hail exist from Gen III. Route 120 and 119 rain powers Water moves; Route 111's sandstorm needs the Go-Goggles to cross.

notes.title: Day care
notes.text: The day care couple on Route 117 raise two Pokémon and make eggs when they get along. Pokémon in the day care gain a level-worth of experience as you walk, but learn moves silently.

notes.title: Moves forgotten and HMs
notes.text: The Move Deleter in Lilycove removes HM moves; the Move Maniac in a Fallarbor house teaches a forgotten level-up move for a Heart Scale.
notes.source: pret/pokeruby LilycoveCity_MoveDeletersHouse, Fallarbor move relearner house (ITEM_HEART_SCALE) scripts

notes.title: Shiny odds
notes.text: A wild or gift Pokémon is shiny with a chance of 8 in 65,536 (about 1 in 8,192). Its colours show in battle and on the summary screen.

notes.title: Mach or Acro Bike
notes.text: Cracked floors (Granite Cave, Sky Pillar) and muddy slopes need the Mach Bike; narrow rails and bunny-hop spots (Route 119, parts of the Safari Zone) need the Acro Bike. Rydel in Mauville swaps them for free.

notes.title: S.S. Tidal
notes.text: After the Hall of Fame the S.S. Tidal sails between Slateport and Lilycove and to the Battle Tower. A hidden Leftovers lies in its lower deck's trash can.
notes.source: pret/pokeruby SSTidal maps (hidden ITEM_LEFTOVERS in SSTidalLowerDeck)

notes.title: Trading with Emerald
notes.text: Ruby and Sapphire trade with Emerald and FireRed/LeafGreen over the Game Link Cable. Emerald has both Seedot and Lotad lines and both Mawile and Sableye.
